div.div: رِيحٌ سَهُوجٌ and سَهْوَجٌ (O, K) and ↓ سَيْهَجٌ (S, O, K) and ↓ سَيْهُوجٌ , (S, A, O, K,) in the last two of which the ج is asserted by Yaakoob to be a substitute for ك, (Az, TA,) and ↓ سَيْهَجَةٌ , (TA,) A violent wind. (S, A, O, K.) And you say also رِيَاحٌ سُهَّجٌ (JK, S, O) and سَاهِجَاتٌ (JK) [both pls. of ↓ رِيحٌ سَاهِجَةٌ , and signifying, accord. to the context in the JK and O, Violent winds: or, accord. to the context in the S, winds that pare the ground: the sing. like رِيحٌ سَهُوكٌ and سَاهِكَةٌ &c.].
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
